laws.rule: Beaches are open from 7 am to sunset; swimming after sunset, driving vehicles on the beach and littering are offences. Swim only between the red-and-yellow flags.

laws.rule: At Goa tourist places covered by the Tourist Places Protection and Maintenance Act, the November 2025 tourism order prohibits consuming liquor in a space where it is not permitted, and breaking glass bottles.

laws.rule: At Goa tourist places covered by the Tourist Places Protection and Maintenance Act, the November 2025 tourism order prohibits cooking in open spaces outside areas permitted for cooking, and littering outside designated waste disposal places.
laws.heading: Goa Tourism Department order dated 21 November 2025, published 11 December 2025

laws.rule: The Goa tourism order of November 2025 prohibits driving unauthorised vehicles on beaches at tourist places covered by the Tourist Places Protection and Maintenance Act.
laws.heading: Goa Tourism Department order dated 21 November 2025, published 11 December 2025

laws.rule: The Goa tourism order of November 2025 prohibits coercing or pestering a tourist to buy goods or services, including obstructing a tourist’s movement or compelling a purchase at tourist places covered by the Act.
laws.heading: Goa Tourism Department order dated 21 November 2025, published 11 December 2025

laws.rule: The Goa Animal Preservation Act 1995, section 7, bans selling or offering for sale beef or beef products in contravention of the Act's slaughter rules, except imported beef from neighbouring States that has a certificate from the competent authority. Slaughter of scheduled animals needs a competent authority's certificate (section 4). Anyone selling beef must register (section 7-A).
laws.penalty_signal: Up to 3 years in jail (section 8). Offences are cognizable and non-bailable.

laws.rule: The Goa Prohibition of Smoking and Spitting Act 1997 bars smoking or spitting in a place of public work or use (section 5), which the Act defines to include restaurants, hotel lounges, bus stands, ferry boats, places of worship and beaches, and in a public service vehicle (section 6). It bars selling or storing tobacco products within 100 metres of a place of worship, school or college (section 9), and selling them to anyone under 21 (section 8). An officer can eject a violator (section 12).
laws.penalty_signal: Sections 5, 6, 9, 10: a fine of up to INR 1,000 (about A$15); a repeat offence a fine of INR 2,000 to 5,000 (about A$30 to A$75). Sections 7 and 8: a fine of up to INR 1,000, and for a repeat offence up to 3 months or a fine of INR 5,000 to 10,000 (about A$75 to A$149), or both.

laws.rule: Under the Goa Excise Duty Act 1964, section 8, no one except a licensed manufacturer or dealer may possess liquor above the quantity the Government sets by notification, except under a Commissioner's permit. Section 5 requires a permit to transport an excisable article above the notified quantity within Goa, but the proviso says none is needed to transport foreign liquor for genuine private consumption unless the Government notifies otherwise for a local area.
laws.penalty_signal: Possessing a contraband excisable article knowing it was unlawfully imported or untaxed (section 33): a fine of up to INR 10,000 (about A$149) or up to 1 year in jail, or both.

laws.rule: Under the Goa Excise Duty Act, 1964, section 19 (as amended in 1976), a licensed vendor or manufacturer, or a person employed by one and acting on their behalf, may not sell or deliver any excisable article or foreign liquor to a person apparently under 21, or to a person of unsound mind. A licence holder may not permit drunkenness, disorderly conduct, riot or gambling in any place where liquor is sold or manufactured.

local-law.note: The 21 November 2025 tourism order supersedes an earlier January 2025 order; current changes after the order should be checked.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Drinking alcohol, taking drugs and smoking are strictly prohibited on all beaches, an offence punishable by a fine, jail or both. Don't drive vehicles on the beach, litter or break bottles. Beaches are open 7 am to sunset; don't swim after sunset, after drinking, or outside the red-and-yellow flagged zones.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Keep away from turtle nesting areas. The leaflet covers beaches only, not temples or churches.

items.text: Under the Goa Excise Duty Act, 1964, section 19 (as amended in 1976), a licensed vendor or manufacturer may not sell or deliver any excisable article or foreign liquor to a person apparently under 21, or to a person of unsound mind. Existing official records also prohibit drinking alcohol on Goa's beaches and, at tourist places covered by the Tourist Places Protection and Maintenance Act, in a space where liquor is not permitted.
